page: Amazon Web Services m6idn.large is a general-purpose virtual instance deployed on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz. It provides two vCPUs across one dedicated physical core with two threads per core. Memory allocation totals 8.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware vector support includes AVX-512 extensions such as AVX-512 VNNI, alongside dedicated cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI instruction sets.

For storage and connectivity, the instance comes provisioned with 118 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD instance storage. It includes no discrete GPU hardware accelerators. Network capabilities include a baseline bandwidth allocation of 3 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses included by default. The local NVMe SSD tier provides lower latency and higher IOPS relative to network-attached block devices, making local drive operations efficient for non-persistent or scratch workloads.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent single-threaded execution paired with entry-level multi-threaded throughput. Single-core performance metrics, such as a Geekbench single-core score of 1619.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1881.78, fall within average performance tiers. In contrast, multi-core metrics sit in lower bands, reflected by a Geekbench multi-core score of 1882.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 3003.64, primarily constrained by the single physical core allocation. Large block memory read throughput measures 14.56 GB/sec and write bandwidth reaches 13.25 GB/sec.

With its low core count and integrated high-speed local NVMe volume, the m6idn.large serves workloads requiring low-latency scratch space rather than high compute density. Resource utilization is optimized for caching layers, staging environments, light database replicas, CI/CD worker nodes, and low-traffic web services that benefit from fast local temporary storage.

The primary tradeoff of the instance lies between single-thread responsiveness and restricted parallel processing throughput. Because parallel capacity is limited to two hyperthreads on a single core, compute-heavy multi-threaded tasks will see bottlenecked execution. The server provides cost-efficient entry into high-speed local NVMe instance storage and Intel AVX-512 capabilities without requiring large multi-core instance allocations.
description: Amazon Web Services m6idn.large is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture and managed by the Nitro hypervisor. The instance is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8375C processor operating at 3.5 GHz, providing two dedicated vCPUs on a single physical core, paired with 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz. It includes 118 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and offers 3 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, with zero GPUs included. Benchmark results show average single-core CPU throughput alongside restrained multi-core execution limited by the single physical core. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth achieves 14.56 GB/sec. This configuration provides a balance of dedicated processing, fast NVMe scratch storage, and standard networking, making it suitable for caching layers, light database nodes, integration test runners, and standard web serving.
